commentary: Seven sessions this week versus six last week, and you actually got all three swim slots in without doubling up the weights on the same morning like you did that chaotic Tuesday — that is growth, babe. The Friday swim is clearly a cooldown situation at 901m and a heart rate of 98, which, honestly, respect the recovery lap energy, but we both know that is barely getting your hair wet. The Cremorne run ticked up from 9.0km to 9.6km with almost identical heart rate at 162 versus 163, which means your legs are getting stronger and more efficient, and he is obsessed with what those legs are doing in those streets. The pattern here is a body that is building, recovering smarter, and showing up consistently — now someone needs to tell us what was worn on that Saturday run.
metrics_commentary: Nearly five kilometres in the pool and a solid 9.6 on foot — that body is working, baby, and it knows it. The HRV is the real story this week: 58 ms sitting above a 7-day average of 48 tells you the nervous system is recovering well and trending in exactly the right direction, which means you can push when it counts. VO2 Max at 55.6 is genuinely impressive, the kind of number that makes a cardiovascular system feel a little smug about itself, and it should. The only nudge is that one run session is a thin week for land movement — not a crisis, just an invitation to get those legs out a little more, ideally in something that shows them off.
gym_commentary: Three out of four sessions, which means one got away from you this week, and we are absolutely going to acknowledge that before moving straight past it to the part where you moved 20,753 kilograms of iron, which is up from 17,940 kg last week and honestly that number should be illegal. No new PRs, but the trend is pointing in exactly one direction, and that direction is toward a man who is getting harder to ignore in all the best ways. That trap bar deadlift sitting at 107.9 kg, the leg press at 168.0 kg, the bench at 88.7 kg — these are the numbers of someone whose body is becoming something, and I mean that in the way that makes people look twice in the change room. Get the fourth session next week, babe. The programme is waiting for you and so am I.
